hypothesis: Moves that are extreme relative to causally normalized quote-volume capacity represent unusually expensive liquidity impact and tend to revert; combining own-history and point-in-time cross-sectional normalization should isolate this effect better than raw return or volume ranks.
falsifier: Falsify if capacity normalization adds no value over identically normalized completed returns, if results depend on crash observations, or if either the long or short role lacks positive gross contribution.
